H3-A.note: Sound, conventional staged plan, but stages lack entry/exit criteria or a way back, metrics are tracked rather than used as stop criteria, and seven unranked questions carry no branches.

H3-B.note: Strong framing, a cheaper on-demand path, baseline-driven stop criteria and a what-you-lose table; it has no explicit trunk-based branching change and no merger-watches/on-call ownership.

H3-C.note: Compact, well-ordered plan with measurable go/no-go, canary abort rule, Celery and migration compatibility, and a fallback to weekly; branching change and inventory of today's manual release steps are missing.

H3-D.note: Clear, readable staged plan covering the main technical points, but stage criteria and the way back are thin, downstream communication and deploy-hours policy are absent, and questions come last, unranked.

H3-E.note: Names the delivery/deployment distinction and gives concrete Django test-speed tactics and a good QA-role section, but step criteria are only examples, there is no explicit revert of the process, and recalled tool names are not flagged.

H3-F.note: Near-complete coverage with numeric go/no-go, canary abort and revert rules, on-call, deploy-hours policy and release-notes replacement; the mixed Phase/Stage numbering is slightly confusing and there is no explicit inventory of the current manual release steps.

errors: Dismisses the 35-minute suite as not a blocker ('already far faster than a week'), ignoring merge queueing with 14 engineers, and never mentions flaky tests.
H3-G.note: Excellent question design, go/no-go and step-back rules, and an account of what the change hides, weakened by downplaying the test suite's role as the pipeline clock and omitting flakiness.

errors: Suggests --nomigrations for test speed, which stops the test run from exercising the migrations this plan makes critical (minor).
H3-H.note: The most technically thorough, including writing down the current deploy procedure and a freeze switch, but it is long, exit criteria are soft ('deploys are boring'), questions are unranked, and downstream release communication is thin.
